title: Heart Sutra 3 San Miguel de Allende
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up the Heart Sutra in San Miguel de Allende, opening with a poem about waking one day to find the walls between people forgotten. Nomon then works through svabhava, the assumed separateness of things, using a piece of paper, a car that won't start, and the mariachi music from the neighbors' construction. Each of the five skandhas gets a plain description, with a friend who is always late as the example for thoughts that grow into stories. A blind-spot card exercise shows the mind filling in what the eye cannot see, and the group reads line three on form and emptiness. Questions on whether emptiness is form's opposite lead to Nomon's closing advice to study one's own suffering.
